image_description: Two distinct clusters of bright yellow coral fungi (Ramaria or similar genus) growing on a forest floor covered in brown leaf litter, pine needles, and patches of green moss. The foreground cluster is larger and more detailed, showing complex branching structures with upright, finger-like tips. The background cluster is slightly out of focus but clearly visible. The lighting is natural and diffuse.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific taxonomic classification of the yellow fungal clusters as 'coral fungus' and rule out look-alikes or AI hallucinations.
To verify the structural integrity of the intricate branching, ensuring no fused branches, floating tips, or boundary bleeding with the background leaf litter.
To assess the naturalness of the texture on the fungal branches and the consistency of the depth of field between the foreground and background clusters.
To ensure the fungi are properly grounded in the leaf litter and not floating, and to check for any geometric distortions in the surrounding debris.

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the tips of the fungal branches in the foreground cluster. AI generators often struggle with fine, repetitive structures, leading to 'melted' or fused tips. Verify if each branch terminates distinctly. Also, check the interface between the fungal base and the brown leaf litter for any unnatural blurring or color bleeding that suggests poor segmentation.
